description:
We are developing hardware modules that detect nearby fires and send early alerts to protect forests, farmland and communities.

Our analytics platform identifies areas at the highest risk of ignition and forecasts fire spread based on weather conditions. Together, they provide a complete solution for early detection and help responders decide where to create firebreaks.

When there is no fire, the modules monitor microclimate conditions in remote areas.
summary:
DrySpell is a web app that turns two generations of NASA satellite fire detections into one consistent fire-activity calendar. MODIS has recorded active fires since 2000; VIIRS is newer and much more sensitive, so simply joining the two records creates a fake jump in activity. We put both on a common 0.25° grid, count detected cell-days per month, and fit one VIIRS-to-MODIS factor per country on Nov 2024 – Jul 2025. On five held-out months (Aug – Dec 2025) disagreement with MODIS fell in all four regions; in Ireland, for example, the error dropped from 3.8 to 1.2. The result is a 312-month calendar (Nov 2000 – Oct 2026) for Ireland, the UK, Spain and France, where any month can be compared with its historical median, with CSV/SVG export.

Around this history we added a 24-hour fire-detection probability map built with NOAA GFS weather, wind-driven spread scenarios for Ireland, and a low-cost ESP32 temperature sensor that streams readings to the map.

This matters because early-warning teams need to know whether a month is truly unusual, or only measured differently.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

DrySpell answers one question for early-warning teams, emergency services, researchers and land managers: "Is this month unusually active, or are we simply measuring it differently?"

1. Harmonized fire calendar (the challenge). MODIS (since Nov 2000, ~1 km) and VIIRS (375 m, more sensitive) detections from NASA FIRMS are mapped to a common 0.25° grid. We count detected grid-cell days (one per cell per day; VIIRS satellites merged so duplicates are not added). For each country we fit one non-negative factor that puts VIIRS on the MODIS scale (Nov 2024 – Jul 2025) and test it on Aug – Dec 2025 without refitting. Mean absolute error vs MODIS on the held-out months: Ireland 3.80 → 1.21, UK 96.80 → 21.24, Spain 305.20 → 52.69, France 188.60 → 24.36. The final series uses MODIS where available and adjusted VIIRS after that; overlapping data is never added. Users choose a region, period and metric (raw MODIS, raw VIIRS or harmonized), compare each month with the median of the same month in 2003–2023, and export monthly CSV, calendar SVG, validation SVG and VIIRS points.

2. Near-term risk. A model (gradient boosting + logistic regression) trained on VIIRS history and NOAA GFS weather gives each 0.25° cell the probability of at least one satellite fire detection in the next 24 hours. The public site shows a saved forecast snapshot (13 Nov 2026).

3. Conditional spread. NOAA GFS 10 m wind shows where a fire could be pushed. For Ireland, a what-if simulation uses real terrain (Copernicus DEM) and land cover (ESA WorldCover) on 25 m cells.

4. Local sensing. An ESP32 temperature sensor sends readings through our receiver and a WebSocket relay to a Ground sensors panel on the map.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

The harmonized value is a MODIS-scale activity index, not a count of fires or burned area. A hot spot is a heat detection, not necessarily a wildfire. Cells dominated by gas flares, industry and volcanoes are masked. Five held-out months are a first check, not proof for every season. The spread simulation is a what-if, not an operational forecast.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, Matplotlib), JavaScript + Leaflet, Node.js (simulation engine, HTTP/WebSocket gateway), ESP32 hardware, Docker on Render.
